newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN, BUT CRITICS HIT TAYLOR FOR SIX.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN, BUT CRITICS HIT TAYLOR FOR SIX.

text.p: Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor found himself in the unusual position on Tuesday of celebrating a stunning test win in South Africa while facing growing calls at home for his immediate sacking.
Australia's memorable fightback to beat South Africa by two wickets in the second test on Monday failed to deflect attention from Taylor's dismal form as a batsman.
The left-handed opener scored only 21 runs in two innings in Port Elizabeth, the latest in a series of failures over the past 15 months that have prompted calls for him to be sacked.
Former Australia test captain Neil Harvey headed the list of critics, saying all-rounder Steve Waugh should take over as captain regardless of Australia's recent successes.
By taking a winning 2-0 lead in the series, Australia strengthened their position as the best test team in the world under a ranking system devised by Wisden Cricketers' Almanack.
Harvey, who played 79 tests for Australia between 1946 and 1962, said Taylor should be removed before the third and final test in Pretoria, starting on Friday.
"My opinion is that he (Taylor) should go. I think he has to come home after this (second) test. He has not been pulling his weight," Harvey told the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper.
Taylor has not scored a test half-century in the past 15 months during which time he has averaged a meagre 17.61 in the test arena.
Those favouring his dismissal argue Taylor should be replaced as opener, thereby strengthening the batting line-up under a new captain.
His supporters say Taylor should be retained because of his outstanding tactical and leadership abilities, giving him time to reverse his slump and keeping a winning side intact.
Kim Hughes, who captained Australia in four spells between 1978 and 1985, said Taylor should be given one more chance to find his form in the third test before selectors act.
"He would need to score runs there, because you can't have a situation were we are one down for not many," Hughes said.
"It's got beyond the stage of being bad luck or a loss of form. There are a couple of technical problems there that don't seem to have been solved. It can't keep going on," Hughes said.
Since Taylor replaced Allan Border as captain in 1994, Australia have won 15 tests, drawn four and lost seven.
During his reign, Australia have beaten West Indies (twice), England, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and South Africa in test series, while losing in Pakistan and India.
His current plight poses a dilemma for Australian selectors, who have traditionally picked their best 11 players before choosing a captain from within their ranks.
Under this system, the captain is expected to hold his place as a batsman or bowler on personal merit.
Former test batsman David Boon, who retired from the international arena last year, suggested a change of approach.
"If the team is winning, it is far easier to carry someone," Boon said. "The opinion as to the quality of his captaincy holds a lot. The guys have been winning -- that's the bottom line."
